text:
The Boltzmann factor for the population ratio of two levels is  

\[
\frac{N_2}{N_1}= \frac{g_2}{g_1}\,e^{-(E_2-E_1)/kT}\; .
\]

The statistical‑weight ratio \(g_2/g_1\) is unchanged, so the change in the ratio is set by the exponential term.  
The energy difference corresponds to a wavelength of \( \lambda \simeq 1448\;\text{Å}\):

\[
\Delta E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}= \frac{1.986\times10^{-25}\,\text{J m}}{1.448\times10^{-7}\,\text{m}}
          \approx 1.37\times10^{-18}\,\text{J}\approx 8.56\;\text{eV}.
\]

Thus  

\[
\frac{\Delta E}{k}= \frac{8.56\;\text{eV}}{8.617\times10^{-5}\,\text{eV K}^{-1}}
                 \approx 9.94\times10^{4}\,\text{K}.
\]

Hence  

\[
\frac{N_2}{N_1}\propto e^{-9.94\times10^{4}/T}.
\]

For the unspotted star (\(T=6000\) K):

\[
\left(\frac{N_2}{N_1}\right)_{6000}=e^{-9.94\times10^{4}/6000}=e^{-16.57}\approx 6.4\times10^{-8}.
\]

For the spotted star the overall effective temperature is \(T_{\rm eff}=5500\) K, so

\[
\left(\frac{N_2}{N_1}\right)_{5500}=e^{-9.94\times10^{4}/5500}=e^{-18.07}\approx 1.4\times10^{-8}.
\]

The factor by which the ratio changes is therefore  

\[
\frac{(N_2/N_1)_{6000}}{(N_2/N_1)_{5500}}
   =\frac{6.4\times10^{-8}}{1.4\times10^{-8}}
   \approx 4.5 .
\]

Thus the observed ratio in the spotless case is about 4.5 times larger than when the star has spots.

**Answer: D**.
